title: Related-Key Security of Hash-Based Re-keying
summary: The proposed re-keying is analyzed in the ideal-cipher model, while standard-model reductions cover only more constrained methods; obtain such a reduction or find a related-key attack.

formal_statement.body: A hash-based re-keying mechanism derives block-cipher keys as $H(K,\mathit{aux})$, where $\mathit{aux}$ may be a short fixed-length value such as a counter, and its security analysis relies heavily on the ideal-cipher model. This reliance implicitly assumes related-key security of the underlying block cipher $E$ for the key relations induced by $H$. Determine whether $E$ remains secure under these induced relations, ideally by giving a standard-model security reduction for this re-keying method, or identify attacks that invalidate the assumption. Existing standard-model results cover only more involved key-derivation methods in a constrained setting where an adversary sequentially queries $B$ blocks under one key before moving to the next.

scope.domain: Related-key cryptanalysis and standard-model security of hash-based block-cipher re-keying.
assumptions: The security analysis uses the ideal-cipher model.
Related-key security of E is implicitly assumed for the key relations induced by H.
parameters: K: master key used by the re-keying mechanism
aux: short fixed-length auxiliary value, such as a counter
H: hash function that derives keys and induces their relations
E: underlying block cipher whose related-key security is at issue
B: number of blocks queried sequentially under one key in the constrained prior model
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether E is secure under the H-induced key relations, ideally through a standard-model reduction, or exhibit attacks that invalidate the assumption.

citations.label: Revisiting AES-GCM-SIV: Multi-user Security, Faster Key Derivation, and Better Bounds

progress.summary: The paper flags that its analysis relies heavily on the ideal-cipher model and therefore implicitly assumes related-key security of the block cipher. It calls for careful assessment and contrasts the proposal with more involved, constrained methods having standard-model reductions.
citation_labels: Priyanka Bose et al., Revisiting AES-GCM-SIV: Multi-user Security, Faster Key Derivation, and Better Bounds
